svg.title: For clarity, the countable compact selection itself introduces no hidden uniformity assumption. If the i-th coordinate lies eventually in a compact set Ki, choose one of its values in Ki and replace its exceptional earlier values by that value. The resulting sequence belongs to the countable compact product Q i Ki, which is compact metrizable in the cases used here. A convergent subsequence in that product converges in every coordinate. The replacements are eventually absent in each fixed coordinate, so the original sequence has the same coordinate limits.
